document.presentationTitle: Clinical Supply Chain Platform Proposal — Lakeshore Health Network

content.title: Clinical Supply Chain Platform Proposal
content.subtitle: Prepared for Lakeshore Health Network — 14 July 2026 — Proposal #CV-2026-0389 — Valid 60 days

content.title: Lakeshore loses an estimated $11.3M a year to expired inventory, emergency procurement, and manual reconciliation — Corvane eliminates 70% of that within 18 months.
content.subtitle: Executive summary
prose: This proposal covers the Corvane Clinical Supply Platform deployed across all 9 Lakeshore hospitals and 34 ambulatory sites, replacing the current combination of Lawson Mobile Supply Chain, spreadsheet-based par management, and manual OR preference-card reconciliation.

The figures in this deck come from the joint discovery completed in June 2026 with Lakeshore's supply chain, perioperative, and IT teams, including a 90-day extract of purchasing, consumption, and waste data from the three largest facilities.

content.title: What discovery found — the cost of the current state
content.subtitle: Based on FY2025 actuals and the 90-day data extract from Mercy Central, St. Anne's, and Lakeshore East
bulletPoints: $4.1M in expired or obsolete inventory written off in FY2025, concentrated in cath lab and OR high-value implants
$3.7M premium paid on emergency and off-contract purchases — 22% of orders bypass the contracted distributor
$2.2M in labor spent on manual cycle counts and OR preference-card reconciliation (roughly 31 FTE-equivalents)
$1.3M in case-cart pick errors and returns; 6.4% of surgical cases delayed more than 10 minutes awaiting supplies
Par levels last reviewed system-wide in 2022; 61% of stocking locations have no consumption-based reorder logic
Three disconnected item masters across the legacy ERP, the OR system, and the pharmacy wholesaler portal
No real-time recall traceability: the March 2026 balloon-catheter recall took 11 days to fully reconcile

content.title: Current state vs. the Corvane platform
content.subtitle: Left: how Lakeshore operates today. Right: the proposed operating model at steady state.
bulletPoints: Manual par counts on paper and spreadsheets, keyed into Lawson nightly — versus RFID and weighted-bin telemetry driving perpetual inventory with 99.2% accuracy
Emergency orders placed by phone to 14 different distributors — versus exception-based procurement routed automatically to contracted sources with approval workflow
OR preference cards updated annually by a central team — versus cards recalibrated monthly from actual case consumption, surgeon by surgeon
Recalls reconciled by emailing spreadsheets to site coordinators — versus lot-level traceability with a system-wide recall report in under 15 minutes
Three item masters maintained by hand — versus one governed catalog synchronized to Lawson, Epic OpTime, and the wholesaler via published APIs
Waste discovered at annual physical inventory — versus expiry dashboards flagging at-risk stock 90, 60, and 30 days out with automated redistribution

content.title: Projected annual impact at steady state
content.subtitle: Conservative case, validated against Corvane's 12 comparable IDN deployments; ramp assumptions on slide 8

content.title: Five-year total cost of ownership — Corvane vs. status quo
content.subtitle: Status quo includes Lawson maintenance, planned RFID pilot spend, and current waste run-rate; $M per fiscal year

content.title: Investment summary — proposed commercial terms
content.subtitle: Three-year subscription, invoiced annually in advance; all figures USD, exclusive of applicable taxes
bulletPoints: Platform subscription (Enterprise tier, 9 hospitals + 34 ambulatory sites) — $1,840,000 per year
Perioperative module (OpTime-integrated case cart and preference-card engine) — $420,000 per year
RFID hardware: 2,340 smart bins, 41 cabinet readers, 18 dock portals — $1,265,000 one-time, Year 1
Implementation and integration services (fixed fee, scope per SOW-1 attached) — $980,000 one-time
Premium support: 24x7 with 1-hour P1 response and a named technical account manager — $190,000 per year
Year 1 total: $4,695,000 — Years 2 and 3: $2,450,000 per year — 3-year TCO: $9,595,000
Multi-year commitment discount already applied: 12% versus annual list; pricing firm through 12 September 2026

content.title: Implementation timeline — 18 months to full deployment
content.subtitle: Mirrors the phasing used at Providence Mountain West (11 hospitals, go-live on schedule in 2025)
bulletPoints: Months 1-2 — Foundation: item-master consolidation, Lawson and Epic OpTime interface build, governance committee stood up
Months 3-5 — Wave 1: Mercy Central goes live (perpetual inventory + procurement); baseline KPIs frozen for the savings guarantee
Months 6-9 — Wave 2: St. Anne's and Lakeshore East live, including full perioperative module and RFID cabinets in cath lab
Months 10-14 — Wave 3: remaining 6 hospitals in paired cohorts; ambulatory sites onboarded via lightweight kanban model
Months 15-18 — Optimization: par recalibration cycle 2, waste-redistribution engine enabled, savings audit with your finance team
Lakeshore commitments: 1 project sponsor, 2 supply chain SMEs at 50%, IT integration resources per the RACI in SOW-1

content.title: Why Corvane — proof, guarantee, and references
content.subtitle: Everything on this slide is contractual or independently verifiable
bulletPoints: Savings guarantee: if audited Year-2 savings fall below $3.0M, Corvane credits 25% of the Year-3 subscription
12 integrated delivery networks live today, including three on Epic OpTime + Lawson — the same stack as Lakeshore
Median deployment: 17 months for 8+ hospital systems; zero go-live postponements in the last 3 years
HITRUST r2 certified, SOC 2 Type II, and HIPAA business associate agreement included in the master agreement
Reference calls arranged with Providence Mountain West and Carilion Group supply chain VPs at your convenience
Named delivery team attached in Appendix B — the same engagement lead who ran the Providence deployment

content.title: Decision requested by 12 September 2026 to hold Wave 1 delivery capacity and FY27 pricing.
content.subtitle: Proposed next steps
prose: Week of 21 July: technical deep-dive with Lakeshore IT on the Epic and Lawson integration architecture. Week of 4 August: commercial and legal review of the master agreement and SOW-1. Week of 18 August: executive readout and reference calls.
